newsitem.title: PERU: Peru Jan-Aug trade deficit falls 13 pct to 1.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Peru Jan-Aug trade deficit falls 13 pct to 1.2 bln.

text.p: Peru's trade deficit fell 13 percent in the first eight months of the year to $1.224 billion from $1.406 billion in the same period last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Saturday.
Exports grew 7.0 percent in the first eight months to $3.895 billion from $3.637 billion in the same period of 1995, the bank said in its weekly report.
Imports rose 2.0 percent to $5.119 billion, compared with $5.043 billion in the same period last year, the bank said.
Peru's commercial deficit more than doubled to $2.115 billion in 1995 from $1.021 billion the previous year.

The central bank report said traditional exports rose eight percent to $2.871 billion in the first eight months, while non- traditional exports were up six percent to $973 percent, and "other" exports fell 26 percent to $52 million.

Of the traditional exports, mining exports grew five percent to $1.772 billion, oil and oil derivative exports rose 54 percent to $244 million, agriculture exports rose 13 percent to $204 million, while fishing exports gained five percent to $651 million.
Among imports, consumer goods rose five percent to $1.177 billion, raw materials were flat at $2.126 billion, while capital goods imports fell two percent to $1.575 billion.
The bank's category of "other" goods saw imports rise 23 percent to $241 million.
